title: The normal locus of a Noetherian domain with a normal principal localization is open (Stacks 0332)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is an integral domain, and suppose there is a nonzero $f\in R$ such that the localization $R_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then the set $U=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R:\ R_{\mathfrak p}\text{ is a normal domain}\}$, where $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is the localization at the prime $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], is open in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0332 (lemma-openness-normal-locus), lines 45442-45480, and its proof (Serre's criterion 031S, finiteness of associated primes 00LC)

proof.text:
Notation. Let $K$ be the fraction field of the domain $R$. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$ the map $R	o R_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective ($r/1=0$ means $ur=0$ for some $u
otin\mathfrak q$, so $r=0$), so $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is a domain, $
eq0$, a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] (localization of the Noetherian ring $R$ at $R\setminus\mathfrak q$). The same holds for $R_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] (with $f
eq0$ in the domain $R$). Regularity, Krull dimension and depth of a local ring are invariant under ring isomorphisms, and an isomorphism of rings carries normal domains to normal domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; we use this tacitly below.

proof.text:
$D(f)\subseteq U$ ('It is clear that the standard open $D(f)$ is contained in $U$'). Let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime with $f
otin\mathfrak p$. Let $\varphi:R	o R_f$ be the localization at $M=\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$ and $N=\varphi(R\setminus\mathfrak p)\subseteq R_f$, a multiplicative subset not containing $0$ (since $\varphi$ is injective and $0
otin R\setminus\mathfrak p$). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] (1), the localization $T=N^{-1}R_f$ is a localization of $R$ at $U'=\{x\in R:\varphi(x)=\varphi(s)\varphi(f^m)	ext{ for some }s
otin\mathfrak p,\ m\ge0\}$. Since $\varphi$ is injective, $x\in U'$ means $x=sf^m$ with $s
otin\mathfrak p$, and as $f
otin\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak p$ is prime this says exactly $x
otin\mathfrak p$; so $U'=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $T\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ as $R$-algebras. Since $R_f$ is a normal domain by hypothesis, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] applied to $R_f$ and $N$ gives that $T\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain, i.e. $\mathfrak p\in U$. Contrapositively: if $\mathfrak q$ is a prime with $R_{\mathfrak q}$ not a normal domain, then $f\in\mathfrak q$.

proof.text: Non-normality goes up along specialization. Let $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ be primes of $R$ with $R_{\mathfrak q}$ not a normal domain; then $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is not a normal domain. Indeed, put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $Q'=\mathfrak qA$, a prime of $A$ whose contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime] (1) the natural map $R_{\mathfrak q}\to A_{Q'}$ is an isomorphism. If $A$ were a normal domain, then $A_{Q'}$, the localization of $A$ at the multiplicative subset $A\setminus Q'\not\ni0$, would be a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], hence so would $R_{\mathfrak q}$, a contradiction.

proof.text: Serre's criterion at a non-normal point. Let $\mathfrak p\notin U$ and $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, a Noetherian local domain (step 1). First, $A$ is not a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: otherwise its localization $A_{\mathfrak pA}$ at the prime $\mathfrak pA$ would be a normal domain, while $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak pA}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime] (1) (with $Q'=\mathfrak pA$, whose contraction is $\mathfrak p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] (1)), so $R_{\mathfrak p}$ would be a normal domain. By Serre's criterion [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal] for the Noetherian ring $A$, $A$ fails $(R_1)$ or $(S_2)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]: there is a prime $Q'\subset A$ such that either (Case II) $\dim(A_{Q'})\le1$ and $A_{Q'}$ is not a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], or (Case I) $\operatorname{depth}(A_{Q'})<\min\{2,\dim(A_{Q'})\}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ be the contraction of $Q'$ to $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] (1); by [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime] (1), $B:=R_{\mathfrak q}\cong A_{Q'}$, so $B$ is a Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB$ in Case I or Case II.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0332, proof, lines 45455-45464: 'By Serre's criterion Lemma [031S] we see that p not in U implies that for some q contained in p we have either Case I ... or Case II ...'

proof.text: $B=R_{\mathfrak q}$ is not a normal domain, hence $f\in\mathfrak q$ ('This in particular also means that $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is not normal, and hence $f\in\mathfrak q$'). Suppose $B$ were a normal domain. Then for every prime $P\subset B$ the localization $B_P$ is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] (multiplicative subset $B\setminus P\not\ni0$), so $B$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], Noetherian by step 1, and has $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal]. Apply these at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB$: by [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime] (1) (for $A=B=R_{\mathfrak q}$ and $Q'=\mathfrak qB$, contraction $\mathfrak q$) $B\cong B_{\mathfrak qB}$, so $B$ is regular if $\dim B\le1$, and $\operatorname{depth}B\ge\min\{2,\dim B\}$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]; this contradicts both Case I and Case II of step 4. So $B$ is not a normal domain, and by step 2, $f\in\mathfrak q$; thus $f/1$ lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB$ and is nonzero (step 1), hence is a nonzerodivisor on the domain $B$.

$\operatorname{depth}(B)\le1$. In Case I, $\operatorname{depth}(B)<\min\{2,\dim B\}\le2$, so $\operatorname{depth}(B)\le1$. In Case II, $(0)$ is an associated prime of the finite $B$-module $B$: $B\neq0$ is a domain, so $\operatorname{Ann}_B(1)=(0)$ and $(0)$ is prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-dim-associated-prime] (Noetherian local ring $B$, $M=B$, $\mathfrak p=(0)$), $\operatorname{depth}(B)\le\dim(B/(0))=\dim B\le1$.

proof.text:
$\mathfrak qB$ is an associated prime of $B/fB$ ('$\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak q})=\operatorname{depth}(R_{\mathfrak q}/fR_{\mathfrak q})+1$'). By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] applied to the Noetherian local ring $B$, the finite module $M=B
eq0$ and the nonzerodivisor $f/1\in\mathfrak qB$ (step 5): $B/fB
eq0$ and $\operatorname{depth}(B/fB)=\operatorname{depth}(B)-1\le0$ (step 6), so $\operatorname{depth}(B/fB)=0$. Suppose $\mathfrak qB$ were not an associated prime of the finite $B$-module $B/fB$ (generated by the class of $1$). By [lem-weil-pbc-nonzerodivisor-if-maximal-not-associated] there is $x\in\mathfrak qB$ which is a nonzerodivisor on $B/fB$; and $(B/fB)/x(B/fB)=B/(f,x)B
eq0$ since $(f,x)B\subseteq\mathfrak qB$. So $x$ is a $B/fB$-regular sequence of length $1$ in $\mathfrak qB$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and $\operatorname{depth}(B/fB)\ge1$ by [def-weil-pbc-depth], a contradiction. Hence there is $w\in B/fB$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_B(w)=\mathfrak qB$.

proof.text: $\mathfrak q$ is an associated prime of the $R$-module $R/fR$. The localization $(R/fR)_{\mathfrak q}$ of the $R$-module $R/fR$ at $R\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is identified with the $R_{\mathfrak q}$-module $B/fB$ by $\bar r/s\mapsto\overline{r/s}$ (well defined and bijective: $\bar r/s=0$ iff $ur\in fR$ for some $u\notin\mathfrak q$, iff $r/s\in fB$). By step 7 there is $w\in(R/fR)_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_{R_{\mathfrak q}}(w)=\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-prime-from-localization] ($R$ Noetherian, $M=R/fR$) there is $z\in R/fR$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0332, proof, lines 45469-45471 (associated primes of R/fR), with Lemma Tag 0310 (lemma-associated-primes-localize) for passing from R_q to R

proof.text: Conclusion ('Thus there is a finite set $E$ of such primes $\mathfrak q$ (see Lemma 00LC) and $\operatorname{Spec}(R)\setminus U=\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\in E}V(\mathfrak q)$'). Let $E$ be the set of primes $\mathfrak q\subset R$ which are associated primes of the $R$-module $R/fR$ and for which $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is not a normal domain. $R/fR$ is a finite $R$-module (generated by the class of $1$) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], so its set of associated primes is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite], and $E$ is finite. If $\mathfrak p\notin U$, steps 4, 5 and 8 give $\mathfrak q\in E$ with $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$, i.e. $\mathfrak p\in V(\mathfrak q)$. Conversely if $\mathfrak p\in V(\mathfrak q)$ with $\mathfrak q\in E$, then $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is not a normal domain, so $\mathfrak p\notin U$ by step 3. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}(R)\setminus U=\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\in E}V(\mathfrak q)$, a finite union of the sets $V(\mathfrak q)=\{\mathfrak p:\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$, which are closed in the Zariski topology of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A finite union of closed sets is closed, so $U$ is open.
